UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA

ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Vv. Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
The Honorable Judge

Rossie D. Alston Jr.

KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

[PROPOSED] ORDER ON PLAINTIFF’S RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS TO ECF NO. 84
AND ON THE PENDING OBJECTIONS CONCERNING ECF NO. 64

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections to ECF No. 84 and
Motion to Set Aside the Amendment and Discovery Denials and for Coordinated Determination of
the Pending Objections (ECF No. __), Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections to ECF Nos. 63-65 and
Motion to Set Aside ECF No. 64 (ECF Nos. 66, 67) with the Memorandum in Support (ECF No.
68), and Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to File Notice of Subsequent Record Development (ECF No.
76). Having considered the objections, the briefing, and the record under Federal Rule of Civil
Procedure 72(a) and 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A), it is hereby

A. Disposition of the Objections
ORDERED that Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84 are SUSTAINED to the extent set

forth in this Order; it is further

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document90-1 Filed 10/13/26 Page 2 of 4 PagelD#
895

ORDERED that the ruling in ECF No. 84 denying Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to File
Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint (ECF No. 59) is SET ASIDE, and the rulings in
ECF No. 84 denying Plaintiff’s motions for leave to serve limited interrogatories before the Rule
26(f) conference (ECF Nos. 15 and 54) are SET ASIDE; it is further

ORDERED that ECF No. 76 is GRANTED; the Notice at ECF No. 76-1 is deemed filed
and has been considered in connection with ECF Nos. 66 and 67; it is further

ORDERED that ECF Nos. 66 and 67 are SUSTAINED to the extent set forth in Part B, and
that every other issue presented in ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 68 not expressly decided in this Order
remains pending and preserved;

B. The Comparison Condition and ECF No. 59
ORDERED that the requirement in ECF No. 64 that Plaintiff provide a comparison of the

proposed pleading against the Complaint (ECF No. 1) is VACATED as a condition of
consideration of ECF No. 59, and that the September 11, 2026 deadline in ECF No. 64 is of no
further effect; it is further

ORDERED that ECF No. 59 is GRANTED under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 15(a)
(2) and 15(d); that the proposed pleading at ECF No. 59-1 is deemed filed as of the date of this
Order as Plaintiff’s Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint and is the operative pleading in
this action; and that the Clerk is DIRECTED to docket ECF No. 59-1 separately as the Second
Amended and Supplemental Complaint; it is further

ORDERED that Defendants shall respond to the Second Amended and Supplemental
Complaint within the time provided by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(a)(3), unless the Court
directs otherwise under the following paragraph; it is further

ORDERED that, within fourteen (14) days of the entry of this Order, each Defendant shall

file a statement advising whether it elects to stand on its pending motion to dismiss (ECF No. 10,

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document90-1 Filed 10/13/26 Page 3 of 4 PagelD#

21, or 45, as applicable) and supporting memorandum as directed to the Second Amended and
Supplemental Complaint, or to file a new response under Rule 15(a)(3). Upon receipt of those
statements the Court will direct any further briefing. ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45 remain pending until
so directed;

C. ECE Nos. 15 and 54

ORDERED that Plaintiff’s motions for leave to serve limited interrogatories before the
Rule 26(f) conference (ECF Nos. 15 and 54) are GRANTED under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure
26(d)(1); that Plaintiff may serve on Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
the three interrogatories set out at ECF No. 15-1, and on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. the four
interrogatories set out at ECF No. 54-1, on the terms stated in those documents; and that each
responding Defendant shall serve its answers under oath, limited to “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to
determine after reasonable inquiry,” within seven (7) calendar days after service of the
interrogatories. This authorization is limited to the interrogatories identified; it does not open
general discovery, and no other discovery is authorized by this Order;

D. Preservation and Transition

ORDERED that nothing in this Order revives ECF No. 26, which remains withdrawn (ECF
No. 62), or affects ECF Nos. 43, 70, and 71; it is further

ORDERED that the objections in ECF Nos. 66 and 67 concerning the generative-artificial-
intelligence provisions of ECF Nos. 63 and 65, the termination of oral argument, and the remote-
appearance motion (ECF No. 41) are not resolved by implication and remain pending; Plaintiff’s
request to restore oral argument on ECF Nos. 15 and 54 is DENIED AS MOOT in light of Part C,
without prejudice to the remaining objections; it is further

ORDERED that the Interim Order entered at ECF No.___ expires upon entry of this Order;

it is further

E. The Fifth Objection and the Financial-Conflict Applications
ORDERED that the fifth objection presented in Plaintiff’s objections to ECF No. 84, which

rests on 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4) and § 455(a) and on the financial disclosure reports submitted as
Exhibits A and B to Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis, is not rejected
by implication by the relief granted in Parts A through D, and that Plaintiff’s Motion for Targeted
Vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84, Withdrawal or Modification of the Magistrate-Judge Referral, and
Related Interim Relief (ECF No. ___) remains pending for determination; it is further

ORDERED that the Court will identify, in its order determining Plaintiff’s Motion for
Targeted Vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84, Withdrawal or Modification of the Magistrate-Judge
Referral, and Related Interim Relief (ECF No.___), which requests presented in the fifth objection
and in that motion are decided, which are reserved, and which are moot because complete relief has
been granted by this Order; and that nothing in this Order treats ownership of the reported interest
during the Magistrate Judge’s participation, or disqualification under 28 U.S.C. § 455, as
established or as rejected.

The Clerk is DIRECTED to send a copy of this Order to Plaintiff at his address of record
and to all counsel of record.

It is so ORDERED.

Alexandria, Virginia
, 2026

Rossie D. Alston, Jr.
United States District Judge
